result.rationale: The handler reads booking.attendees, filters uniqueGuests against them, then calls prisma.booking.update with createMany — all outside any transaction or upsert with a unique constraint. Two concurrent addGuests requests can both pass the uniqueness check and insert duplicate attendee rows. No transaction or constraint is visible in the diff to prevent this, so the race is real though only triggerable under concurrency.

judged_text: Race condition on concurrent addGuests requests: non-transactional check-then-write can insert duplicate attendees

record.issue_text: Race condition on concurrent addGuests requests: non-transactional check-then-write can insert duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler reads current attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, then performs a separate write using `prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }})` with no transaction/locking and no `skipDuplicates`. Two concurrent `addGuests` calls can both observe the same pre-state (guest email not yet present) and both insert the same attendee row, leading to duplicates (or a DB error if a unique constraint exists, which is not shown in the diff).
